content:
alex: kicking off the 'stitch' release in ~2h. need to confirm cross-service sequence and blockers: API -> runtime -> console -> router. planning a rolling splice across regions. calling out any hard deps now.

sam: router schema bumped to 1.4.2 (header layout tweak). runtime still on 1.4.1 in a few pools. could cause header parsing mismatch.

jin: we have a small fallback shim that accepts both header layouts. can enable shim for the window (cost: small CPU).

alex: add shim to the rollout plan. also we need explicit rollback gates and release notes updated. @deploybot, can you schedule a wave?

deploybot: deploy scheduled: wave=stitch-2, start=1762349370 (approx +2h), services=[api,runtime,console,router], max_parallel=2, dry_run_window=30m

ops-runner: proposing rollback criteria: if 5xx rate > 1% sustained over 5m OR p95 latency > 400ms for 10m -> pause wave and roll back to stable tag v2026-03-19. logging that here.

sam: console team — confirm UI fields are backward-compatible with API header shim? @jin

jin: console has migration flag 'stitch-ui' behind a feature flag. we'll keep it off until router confirmed at 1.4.2.

alex: release notes draft: https://redwood.internal/notes/stitch-1762345670 — add bullets: shim enabled, runtime pinned, rollback steps. keep it short.

sam: request: can we pin runtime image to v1.12.3 for this wave to avoid any hot-path changes?

alex: yes. pin runtime pool for wave. ops-runner to execute.

ops-runner: pinned runtime pool 'stitch-pool' -> v1.12.3. documented in infra/playbooks/stitch-pin.md.

jin: preflight check: /scripts/smoke-stitch.sh passes locally. recommend a regional dry-run (canary) 30m before full wave.

alex: agreed. plan: 1) add shim to rollout 2) pin runtime 3) run regional dry-run 30m before 4) update release notes 5) set deploybot health probes + rollback hooks.

sam: +1 :+1:

jin: :thumbsup:

deploybot: preflight webhook registered: https://deploybot.internal/hooks/1762345670 — will post progress and pause signals.

alex: thanks. I'll run the dry-run and report back here with metrics. if anything flares, we'll abort and follow rollback doc.
